items.corrections: A root cause and one-time reversal therapy for established Alzheimer disease/tauopathies was not demonstrated by this bounded audit. The relevant phase 3 trial page was found but inaccessible.

Specific human neurostimulation/neuroprosthesis studies for motor-complete injury were found, but their articles could not be read in this audit; no full spinal-cord regeneration claim is substantiated.
A randomized trial examined autologous HSCT as an immune-reset strategy for highly active relapsing-remitting MS. It does not establish a safe complete cure or full CNS remyelination.

Rat implant-response experiment documents persistent inflammation and adjacent neuronal loss, explicitly identifying an unresolved mechanism of chronic recording failure. It supports the biocompatibility research challenge, not long-lived zero-response interface performance.

A 40-athlete postmortem CTE study characterizes stage-associated tau distribution and clinical-history correlations. The second preprint page could not be independently read and is excluded; no causal closure or reversal is demonstrated.

The bounded search did not locate an inspectable primary result for a universal acute-stroke neuroprotectant producing near-zero infarct volume. No such efficacy or the downstream impact forecast is supported here.

A randomized trial of responsive thalamic stimulation for drug-resistant generalized epilepsy was found but the primary page was blocked. No permanent non-destructive cure was established by readable evidence.

A primary single-patient report describes improved residual visual function during a cortical-stimulation study after optic-nerve injury. This unexpected case does not show predictable restoration or near-normal vision.
The bounded search did not substantiate a single transdiagnostic autism mechanism that can be safely normalized in all individuals or a cure after childhood. The impact claim remains unsubstantiated.

The bounded search found no inspectable primary result establishing one pathway that reverses neuronal loss across Parkinson disease, ALS, and FTD. Cross-disease reversal and impact are unsupported here.
